PepsiCo vs. Starbucks: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool

PEP
SBUX
WMT

Trading disclosure

Choosing between PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP) and Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX) often comes down to a choice between stability and growth. Both companies dominate their respective corners of the grocery aisle and the corner coffee shop.

PepsiCo operates a diversified portfolio of snack and beverage brands that reach consumers in over 200 countries. Starbucks relies on its premium brand experience and global retail network to drive customer loyalty. While both are consumer powerhouses, their financial health and valuation profiles offer distinct paths for investors looking to add resilient businesses to their holdings.

The case for PepsiCo

PepsiCo is a titan among beverage stocks and food producers. The company sells a wide range of products, including Frito-Lay snacks and Quaker foods, as well as its namesake soda brands. A significant portion of its success depends on relationships with major retailers like Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT). In 2025, Walmart and its affiliates accounted for approximately 14% of PepsiCo's consolidated net revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, the company reported revenue of nearly $93.9 billion. This represents revenue growth of roughly 2.3% compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was approximately $8.2 billion, down from $9.6 billion reported in FY 2024. Despite this dip, the company continues to benefit from its ability to bundle snacks and drinks across diverse global markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 2.4x. This metric compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a company funds its growth. The current ratio is roughly 0.9x, which measures a company's ability to pay its short-term debts with its short-term assets. Free cash flow for the year reached nearly $7.7 billion, calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures.

The case for Starbucks

Starbucks maintains a dominant position in the global retail coffee market through its network of over 40,000 stores. The company generates revenue primarily through its own retail locations and a growing Channel Development segment. It also benefits from the Global Coffee Alliance with Nestlé (OTC:NSRGF), which distributes Starbucks-branded goods outside traditional coffee shops. This hybrid model of company-operated and licensed stores allows the company to scale efficiently while maintaining brand control.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, Starbucks reported revenue of approximately $37.2 billion. This reflects revenue growth of nearly 2.8% over the previous fiscal year. Net income was close to $1.9 billion, marking a significant decline from the $3.8 billion earned in FY 2024. The net margin compressed to roughly 5% during this period, indicating higher operational costs and shifting consumer spending patterns.

Musk projected SpaceX (SPCX) could hit a $500 billion to $1 trillion annual revenue run rate by end of 2027.

The $1 trillion upper end would top Amazon (AMZN) at $717 billion and Walmart (WMT) at $713 billion in reported annual revenue.

Grokbot surpassed 800,000 paid weekly users, more than doubling in a month, and Musk said it may consume most of SpaceX's superintelligence compute.

Elon Musk gave investors a striking new revenue projection. On the October 20, 2026 third-quarter earnings call for SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), Musk said: "I mean, in a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of [2027] is somewhere between $500 billion and a trillion."

Shutterstock
SPCX Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

He then added, "On that crazy note, I don't want to give Bret a heart attack," a reference to CFO Bret Johnson. Annual recurring revenue is a run rate: one period of current revenue annualized. It measures where the business is heading at a single moment, distinct from a full year of booked sales.

A Steep Climb From Today's Run Rate

On the same call, Bret Johnson said SpaceX remains on track for $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by the end of this year, defined as December revenue annualized. Third-quarter revenue came in at $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion a year earlier. Reaching the low end of Musk's range means the run rate has to grow again within roughly 12 months of SpaceX crossing $100 billion. Wall Street currently estimates SpaceX will book $315 billion in sales in 2028 and $626 billion by 2030, so as usual, Musk is thinking a lot more optimistically than consensus.

CVS Health (CVS) stock has returned 24.3% over the past six months, compared with 9.8% for the S&P 500. In August, CVS raised its 2026 profit forecast. On the same August call, the company warned that its 340B business will be a headwind in 2027 and that it expects Caremark to lose members, partly because some health plan customers are cutting products and leaving markets.

Either way

CVS Health's First Look At 2027 On November 4

CVS is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2026 results on or around November 4, 2026. The company said it would use the call to outline headwinds and tailwinds for 2027. Investors will get the full 2027 guidance during the fiscal Q4 2026 call, expected on or around February 8, 2027. In August, executives said an outlook of at least $8.44 of adjusted earnings per share for 2027 looked reasonable. They called this about 13% growth off an adjusted baseline of $7.46. The company offered that view on the same call where it flagged the 340B and Caremark pressures. On November 4, watch the size executives put on each 2027 headwind they name.

The dates ahead matter most when CVS Health is a large share of what you own. See how to protect a concentrated position.

The 340B Headwind In Pharmacy Services

CVS expects the market dynamics in its 340B business to continue and become a headwind for its Pharmacy Services business in 2027. During the fiscal Q2 2026 call, executives said that drugmakers are imposing restrictions on covered entities, and that this led to some of the pressure CVS saw in that quarter. When asked how the company would offset the headwind, leadership pointed to the specialty pharmacy business, which they said continues to perform exceptionally well. They added that CVS Specialty patients stick to their medicines at a rate above 90%, compared with an industry standard of 80%. The company declined to size the 340B headwind at the time, so on November 4 watch whether executives now put a number on it.

Chicago, IL – October 21, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Vicor VICR as the Bull of the Day and NIKE NKE as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on Walmart Inc. WMT, Target Corp. TGT and Costco Wholesale Corp. COST.

Here is a synopsis of all five stocks:

Bull of the Day:

Throughout the AI boom, we have seen a steady stream of niche technology companies emerge as critical players in the infrastructure buildout. What began with GPUs and custom semiconductors has expanded into memory, optical networking, advanced packaging and a growing list of other industries.

While there are certainly still opportunities across those segments, I am particularly interested in identifying the next wave of beneficiaries. One emerging opportunity is in power delivery, as AI data centers are beginning to fundamentally rethink how electricity gets from the grid to increasingly powerful processors.

The problem is straightforward. AI systems are becoming so powerful and energy-intensive that traditional data center electrical infrastructure is struggling to keep up. Some next-generation server racks are expected to require as much as one megawatt of electricity, creating enormous challenges in efficiently delivering that power without wasting energy, generating excess heat or consuming valuable space.

To address these challenges, the industry is moving toward a new 800-volt direct current (DC) power architecture, which allows electricity to travel through data centers more efficiently and with fewer conversion steps.

Vicor() develops highly efficient power conversion modules that help deliver electricity at the precise voltage required by advanced processors. Its technology becomes increasingly valuable as AI chips demand more power in less space, positioning the company to benefit from the industry's shift toward higher-density computing.

The company also carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), supported by an increasingly bullish earnings outlook.

Adding to the investment case, Vicor reported outstanding quarterly results Tuesday morning, with revenue surging nearly 79% year over year and profitability improving dramatically. Shares rallied following the announcement, reinforcing the company's accelerating fundamental momentum.

Despite a powerful rally earlier this year, VICR has since undergone a sharp correction and remains roughly 46% below its previous highs. With an emerging industry tailwind, exceptional growth forecasts and a top Zacks Rank, Vicor stands out as a compelling opportunity in the next phase of the AI infrastructure buildout.

The shares climbed 14.23% to €138.10, their highest level since July 7, while France's CAC 40 fell 0.52%.

Revenue on an adjusted basis, which excludes certain non-cash accounting adjustments relating to its Walmart contract, rose 25.2% to €445 million. Order entries rose 10% year on year to €462 million, the highest third-quarter total in the company's history, supported by major retailer contracts in Europe and additional projects in North America.

Software and services continued to expand rapidly. Revenue from value-added services (VAS) increased 40% to €202 million in the first nine months of the year, including recurring revenue that jumped 77% to €100 million. Annualised recurring revenue reached €154 million at the end of September, up 82% year on year.

VusionGroup maintained its 2026 targets, including adjusted revenue growth of 15% to 20% at constant exchange rates and tariffs, VAS revenue growth of around 40%, and an increase of more than 100 basis points in its adjusted EBITDA margin.

Chief Executive Thierry Gadou said the quarter reflected continued customer expansion, improving momentum in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and new North American agreements. VusionGroup plans to outline its medium-term strategy and growth ambitions at a Capital Markets Day in Paris on November 18.
